focus: Foundational papers on retrieval-augmented and long-context generation with citations and on atomic-claim factuality evaluation of long-form generated text
context: Hook: Curated knowledge bases such as OMIM are built by experts who read papers and record, entry by entry, what each paper showed; language models can now read those papers, and many system designs (long-context reading, extraction into graphs or tables, agents, draft-then-verify, prompt optimisation) have been proposed for turning documents into structured, cited text, but they were evaluated on different tasks, models, retrieval stacks and scoring, so their results cannot be compared.. Gap: There is no controlled evaluation in which the cited sources, the model, the mechanical guards and the scoring are held fixed and only the generation strategy varies, scored against curator-written per-paper text and structured fields. Scoped to what the log evaluates: one model family, 100 small OMIM phenotype entries (2-12 references) given the curators' own reference list, open-access text only; questions are (1) how much the strategy matters, (2) whether the strategy or what it could read limits agreement with curators, and (3) what a claim-level audit against the cited source can and cannot catch. No claim of generality across models, of clinical use, or of human validation.

section: Related Work: 2.1 Language models for literature curation in genetics and biology
focus: LLM gene-disease-phenotype extraction full-text human genetics literature benchmark
context: Mission: Find work up to 2026-11 that uses language models to populate or assist curated biological knowledge bases (FlyBase/GO-style annotation, HPO annotation, ClinVar/variant evidence, gene-disease validity, rare-disease profiles), with emphasis on how each is evaluated: what reference, whether sources are fixed, whether curator-written text is used. Include the closest prior work named in notes.md (FlyAOC, GEN-KnowRD, WikiCrow, Groza et al. 2026) and phenotype concept-recognition baselines. Do not look for new systems to compare against; none were run.. Hypothesis: Prior work varies the retrieval, the model and the scoring together, scores against structured annotations or encyclopedia text rather than curators' per-paper prose, or tests what the model remembers rather than what it reads; none holds the cited papers fixed and varies only the generation strategy.

section: Related Work: 2.2 Intermediate representations versus long-context reading
focus: RAG versus long-context LLM systematic comparison
context: Mission: Collect systematic comparisons of long-context reading with RAG and GraphRAG, document-processing pipelines that extract to structured intermediates (graphs, tables, databases with reconciliation), and agentic literature-synthesis systems that write cited articles, up to 2026-11. Focus on what each compared and on which tasks; note where comparisons conflate model, retrieval and scoring.. Hypothesis: Evidence on whether an intermediate representation helps over reading the documents directly is mixed and task-dependent, comes from QA or summarisation tasks rather than knowledge-base writing, and rarely includes matched ablations that separate the representation from other design choices such as extraction effort.

section: Related Work: 2.3 Memory, verification and contamination
context: Mission: Find work on generating from model memory and then verifying (chain-of-verification, self-verification against databases), and on detecting or measuring benchmark contamination (time-based splits, black-box tests), up to 2026-11. Look for evidence on whether verification after recall adds content or only removes/corrects it.. Hypothesis: Verify-after-recall methods are mostly evaluated on short-form or general-knowledge tasks where memory is strong; contamination studies rarely provide a control that measures what memory alone supplies for the same task and how this changes with when the knowledge was created.

section: Related Work: 2.4 Supervision by prompt optimisation
focus: reflective prompt evolution outperforms reinforcement learning
context: Mission: Find prompt-optimisation and reflective prompt-evolution methods (up to 2026-11) and their reported sample efficiency and evaluation settings, to position a small learned curation guide (two reflection rounds on 27 training entries).. Hypothesis: Prompt optimisation results are reported with substantial search budgets and on tasks with dense, cheap feedback; little is known about whether a guide learned from omissions and extras transfers to long-form knowledge-base writing with expensive scoring.

section: 3. Benchmark and Strategies - 3.1 Task, entries and reference
focus: research paper or technical report introducing 'mim2gene' (OMIM-to-NCBI Gene mapping)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Formalise as in idea.md 'Formal setup': entry e = (h, R), R = {d_1,...,d_n}, access level a(d) in {full text, abstract, title}; strategy S maps (h, R) to draft D (paragraphs citing non-empty subsets of R, genes, inheritance modes, ontology terms, variants). Input: entry number, title and alternative titles plus exactly the cited papers; causal gene withheld (idea.md 'Design rationale'). Entries: 100 drawn at random with a fixed seed, 20 per creation-era band of entry number; eligibility 2-12 references, causal gene in gene map, >=5 phenotype annotations, >=1 in-scope curator paragraph; sample is stratified and selects well-annotated, molecularly characterised entries (log Sec. 1.1). Papers: 515 cited; readable in full 96 (19%), abstract only 345, title only 74; open access via PubMed Central or Europe PMC; supplementary material not retrieved (log Sec. 1.1). Reference with required wording (notes.md 'Words to use'): 'OMIM facts conveyed' = coverage of facts in OMIM's allelic-variant descriptions as deposited in ClinVar, from OMIM's gene entries, variant-centred; 476 paragraphs in scope; split once into 6,652 fixed facts without sight of any draft. Narrative sections of phenotype entries are not compared. Clinical synopsis reference = HPO disease annotations: 2,311, of which 1,835 are the HPO team's own curation from papers and 476 taken from OMIM; never call it OMIM's synopsis. Causal gene from OMIM gene map via MedGen and mim2gene; inheritance from HPO and MedGen as coarse classes; 427 in-scope OMIM-submitted ClinVar variants (log Sec. 1.1). Other evaluation sets: 40-entry ablation subset, 30-entry replicate subset, 12 entries with 30-75 references (exploratory), 30 entries created June-November 2026 (log Sec. 1.1).

focus: technical report or documentation introducing 'Claude Code'
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Present Table 1 from log Sec. 1.3: three paradigms (Read and write: direct reading as baseline, agentic curator; Extract, then write: evidence graph, case table first; Memory first: recall, then verify), the memory-only control, and add-ons each tested against its parent (second-hand evidence and learned curation guide on direct reading; reconciled case database on the case table). Describe each strategy only as in log Sec. 1.3 and idea.md 'Core idea'; note evidence-graph findings with quotes not found in the paper are discarded (none were in this run; log Sec. 2.13) and agentic curator quotes were all found verbatim (2,600; self-reported opening; log Sec. 2.13). State that recall, then verify may not add content from the papers, so its low coverage is partly by construction (log Sec. 1.3, 12). Model and settings: one model (Claude Opus 5.5) via the Claude Code command-line interface in headless mode with schema-constrained output; no temperature or seed exposed; reasoning effort high for writers, medium for per-paper extraction, audit and judging; no web access; replies cached so each call is made once (log Sec. 1.2). Replies 'stopped by the model's safety filter' are recorded, never retried with a changed prompt; reasons not visible (log Sec. 1.2; notes.md). Mechanical guards applied to every strategy: ontology identifiers chosen only from ontology-search candidates; gene symbols normalised against HGNC; recalled cross-reference numbers removed; every paragraph must cite a supplied paper (log Sec. 1.3; idea.md 'Design rationale'). Say 'our extract-then-write implementations'; published systems (e.g. SLIDERS, PaperQA2) were not run; strategies are our implementations of the ideas (log Sec. 12).
